name: Sebastian Selman
role: Data & Analytics in organisations · Teaching, talks, podcast
tagline: I work on the gap between what technology can do and what organisations manage to do with it.
offer: I teach and speak about it: guest lectures and workshops for universities and programmes, talks for conferences, and conversations on podcasts.
intro: That gap is mostly not technical. It shows up as a data platform nobody trusts, a governance model written for a world that no longer exists, or an AI pilot that works beautifully and changes nothing. I spend my time on the organisational side of that problem — currently in enterprise data engineering and data governance, previously across Microsoft's Azure data and AI portfolio, and before that as a design-thinking consultant working with banks and healthcare on how they actually make decisions.

I teach some of this: four years lecturing on digital corporate culture at BVS St. Gallen, and a run of workshops and sessions with universities and fellowship programmes. I co-host a podcast about what happens when enterprises put AI into production, and I write — sometimes about Azure and data architecture, sometimes about borders, personas and why IKEA sells hot dogs.
I grew up in Baden-Baden, was born in Toronto, and started my working life as assistant to a violin maker in Tübingen. Some of that turns out to be more relevant than it sounds.

invite.heading: Invite me
invite.intro: If you run a course, a programme, a conference or a podcast, and the gap between what data and analytics can do and what organisations do with it belongs on your agenda, I would like to hear from you.

formats.name: Guest lecture
formats.line: A session for a course or degree programme on how organisations actually adopt data and analytics, and why the technology is rarely the hard part.
formats.evidence: Four years lecturing Digital Corporate Culture on the Dipl. Digital Innovation Manager NDS HF programme at BVS St. Gallen (2020–2024).

formats.name: Workshop
formats.line: Hands-on, for a cohort or a team: participants build something that works before they discuss what it means.
formats.evidence: Slaying Dragons with AI, built with Franziska-J. Klebôn: run at Tomorrow University in Berlin (40 attendees), the WAVE Fellowship and HeadsQuarter Zurich. Earlier: lead coach on EY's Innovation Journey, training around a thousand colleagues.

formats.name: Talk or keynote
formats.line: For a conference, leadership event or offsite: why a data platform nobody trusts changes nothing, and what makes data actually used.
formats.evidence: Two live sessions in November 2026: hosting an expert panel on SAP data in Microsoft Fabric, and co-presenting AI in event management with Nico Bühler of Alibaba Cloud.

formats.name: Podcast guest
formats.line: Happy to sit on the other side of the microphone, for shows on data, analytics, work and how organisations change.
formats.evidence: Co-host of Business Mission Control with Dr. Estera Kot since April 2026: conversations on what happens when enterprises put AI into production.
